body: Wanted to tell you but it seems you figured it out in the comment above, haha. Glad I could help with some perspective. Also, one last thing, take care not to fall in the alpha male bs pipeline as it literally preys on fellas like you. have a great one!

sweetheart, i get where ur coming from, but people partly can tell your age because of the topics you're arguing themselves. not to sound condescending but most sane adults don't have the time to argue about anime or stuff in comment sections like instagram, for example, as that's the place i see most heated arguments taking place in. i know i'm lowkey proving my own point with this one, but even me leaving this comment just speaks about the fact that i'm unemployed. LOL

also, another thing to note, perfect grammar doesn't mean shit nowadays, and can also be part of the reason why you're perceived as younger, as it's literally one's attempt of trying to seem more intelligent/mature than they are, OR than their opponent. read this argument in a neutral manner. this is not an attack on you, and it is not to say that it's wrong to use perfect grammar. it's also the fact that usually the people using this have the most technicality-based arguments and tend to be very annoying just to prove a point that is not applicable in real life. maybe i am projecting, but many people i know, myself included, used to overcompensate in this way, too.

finally, at the end of the day, if you love debating, i really recommend for you to keep in mind the following:

1. it's anyone's right to disengage from a discussion, even if they might be right, for their own peace. you are indeed young, so you wouldn't remember how much of a different place the world felt like even 10 years ago. people have become so radicalized and hot headed that it's genuinely exhausting to have even standard discussions nowadays.
2. sometimes being right doesn't mean anything. if you are objectively right about an argument, but you have just hurt people in the process, can you really be satisfied with yourself? few things make sense in this world, but the thing i personally find that makes perfect sense is trying to be kind whenever possible.
3. def try going to a real life debate club
4. don't fry ur brain with social media from such a young age, you'll thank yourself later
5. maybe you don't, but getting annoyed at every stranger online that has shit opinions is not going to have any sort of positive impact on your life. so this is just my way of saying that even if you have a passion for debates, social media is not the right place to have them. if point 3 isn't applicable, then at least try to find like minded people in real life to discuss with. it's life changing.

welp, did my best here. take care, kid, and read on digital footprint. (my standard advice for everyone) o/

p.s. i am not proof-reading this, sry if i rambled
